questions.q: Two blocks of masses $W_1$ and $W_2$ are suspended from the ends of a light string passing over a smooth fixed pulley. If the pulley is pulled up with an acceleration ' $\mathrm{g}$ ', then the tension in the string will be
questions.solution: For mass $\mathrm{W}_1$ \begin{aligned} & \mathrm{W}_1 \mathrm{a}-\mathrm{W}_1 a_0=\mathrm{W}_1 \mathrm{~g}-\mathrm{T} \\ & \mathrm{W}_1 \mathrm{a}-\mathrm{W}_1 \mathrm{~g}=\mathrm{W}_1 \mathrm{~g}-\mathrm{T} \\ & \mathrm{W}_1 \mathrm{a}=2 \mathrm{~W}_1 \mathrm{~g}-\mathrm{T} \end{aligned} For mass $\mathrm{W}_2$ \begin{aligned} & \mathrm{W}_2 \mathrm{a}+\mathrm{W}_2 \mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{o}}=\mathrm{T}-\mathrm{W}_2 \mathrm{~g} \\ & \mathrm{~W}_2 \mathrm{a}+\mathrm{W}_2 \mathrm{~g}=\mathrm{T}-\mathrm{W}_2 \mathrm{~g} \\ & \mathrm{~W}_2 \mathrm{a}=\mathrm{T}-2 \mathrm{~W}_2 \mathrm{~g} \end{aligned} Adding equation (i) and (ii), We have \begin{aligned} & \mathrm{W}_1 \mathrm{a}+\mathrm{W}_2 \mathrm{a}=2 \mathrm{~W}_1 \mathrm{~g}-2 \mathrm{~W}_2 \mathrm{~g} \\ & \mathrm{a}=\frac{2 \mathrm{~g}\left(\mathrm{~W}_1-\mathrm{W}_2\right)}{\mathrm{W}_1+\mathrm{W}_2} \end{aligned} Put this value in equation (i) \begin{aligned} & \mathrm{W}_1 \times \frac{2 \mathrm{~g}\left(\mathrm{~W}_1-\mathrm{W}_2\right)}{\mathrm{W}_1+\mathrm{W}_2}=2 \mathrm{~W}_1 \mathrm{~g}-\mathrm{T} \\ & \frac{2 \mathrm{gW}_1^2}{\mathrm{~W}_1+\mathrm{W}_2}-\frac{2 \mathrm{gW}_1 \mathrm{~W}_2}{\mathrm{~W}_1+\mathrm{W}_2}=2 \mathrm{~W}_1 \mathrm{~g}-\mathrm{T} \\ & \mathrm{T}=2 \mathrm{~W}_1 \mathrm{~g}-\frac{2 \mathrm{gW}_1^2}{\mathrm{~W}_1+\mathrm{W}_2}+\frac{2 \mathrm{gW}_1 \mathrm{~W}_2}{\mathrm{~W}_1+\mathrm{W}_2} \\ & =\frac{2 \mathrm{~g}\left[\mathrm{~W}_1^2+\mathrm{W}_1 \mathrm{~W}_2-\mathrm{W}_1^2+\mathrm{W}_1 \mathrm{~W}_2\right]}{\mathrm{W}_1+\mathrm{W}_2} \\ & =\frac{4 \mathrm{~W}_1 \mathrm{~W}_2 \mathrm{~g}}{\mathrm{~W}_1+\mathrm{W}_2} \end{aligned}

questions.solution:
Period of oscillation of a bar, $\mathrm{T}_1=2 \mathrm{~s}$

& \mathrm{T}=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{I}}{\mathrm{MH}}} \\

& \Rightarrow \frac{2}{\mathrm{~T}_2}=2 \\
& \Rightarrow \mathrm{T}_2=1 \mathrm{~s} .
\end{aligned}

Velocity of bird flies, $\mathrm{v}=|\mathrm{t}-2| \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}$ at $\mathrm{t}=0 \mathrm{~s}, \mathrm{v}=2 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$
at $\mathrm{t}=2 \mathrm{~s}, \mathrm{v}=0 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$

\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{s}_2=\mathrm{v}(\Delta \mathrm{t})+\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{a}_2(\Delta \mathrm{t})^2 \\

& =0 \times 4+\frac{1}{2} \times 1 \times 2^2 \\
& =2
\end{aligned}

$\begin{aligned} & \text { Total distance }=s_1+s_2 \\ & =2+2=4 m\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The efficiency of an engine is given by $\eta=\frac{\alpha \beta}{\sin \theta} \cdot \log _{\mathrm{e}} \frac{\beta \mathrm{x}}{\mathrm{kT}}$, where $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are constants. If $T$ is the absolute temperature, $k$ - Boltzmann constant, $\theta$-angular displacement and $\mathbf{x}$ is distance, then the incorrect statement is
options: Dimensions of $\beta$ are same as that of force
Dimensions of $\alpha^{-1} \mathrm{x}$ are same as that of energy
Dimensions of $\eta^{-1} \sin \theta$ are same as that of $\alpha \beta$
Dimensions of $\alpha$ are same as that of $\beta$
questions.solution:
The efficiency of an engine is given by
$\begin{aligned} \\ & \eta=\frac{\alpha \beta}{\sin \theta} \log _{\mathrm{e}} \frac{\beta \mathrm{x}}{\mathrm{kT}} \\ \\ & {[\alpha \beta]=[\eta]=[\sin \theta]=\text { Dimension less }} \\ \\ & {\left[\eta^{-1} \sin \theta\right]=[\alpha \cdot \beta]=\text { Dimension less }} \\ \\ & \frac{\beta \mathrm{x}}{\mathrm{kt}}=1 \\ \\ & \beta=\frac{\mathrm{kT}}{\mathrm{x}} \\ \end{aligned}$
Here, Boltzmann constant, $\mathrm{K}=\left[\mathrm{ML}^2 \mathrm{~T}^{-2} \mathrm{~K}^{-1}\right]$
$\begin{aligned} \\ & \beta=\frac{\left[\mathrm{ML}^2 \mathrm{~T}^{-2} \mathrm{~K}^{-1}\right][\mathrm{K}]}{[\mathrm{L}]} \\ \\ & =\left[\mathrm{ML} \mathrm{T}^{-2}\right] \\ \end{aligned}$
Force, $\mathrm{F}=\mathrm{ma}=\mathrm{m} \frac{\mathrm{dv}}{\mathrm{dt}}$
Force, $\mathrm{F}=\left[\mathrm{ML} \mathrm{T}^{-2}\right]$
Hence, Dimension of $\beta$ are same as that of force.
$\begin{aligned} \\ & \beta=\alpha^{-1}=\left[\mathrm{ML} \mathrm{T}^{-2}\right] \\ \\ & \alpha^{-1} \mathrm{x}=\left[\mathrm{ML} \mathrm{T}^{-2}\right][\mathrm{L}]=\left[\mathrm{ML}^2 \mathrm{~T}^{-2}\right] \\ \end{aligned}$
Energy, $\mathrm{E}=\mathrm{mc}^2=\mathrm{ML}^2 \mathrm{~T}^{-2}$
Hence, dimension of $\alpha^{-1} \mathrm{x}$ are same as that of energy.
